views.name: v_anchor_changes
views.description: A move: a number's anchor changes from one cell site to a different one that then holds for at least hold_weeks weeks (set by the application from the question; 2 when it names none), reported at the first week of the new anchor, with the distance in kilometres between the two cell sites. One row per move per slot (night: where it sleeps, day: where it spends weekdays). CELL SITES, NOT POSITIONS OF A PERSON.

columns.name: number
columns.description: The number that moved.

columns.name: slot
columns.description: night (where it sleeps) or day (where it spends weekdays).

columns.name: from_cell_key
columns.description: The cell site of the anchor before the move.

columns.name: to_cell_key
columns.description: The cell site of the anchor after the move.

columns.name: first_week
columns.description: The first week of the new anchor (counted from the start of the case): when the move shows.

columns.name: first_week_start
columns.description: The date on which that week starts.

columns.name: distance_km
columns.description: Distance in kilometres between the two cell sites, empty when a site has no position.

columns.name: hold_weeks
columns.description: The weeks the new anchor must hold to count as a move, set by the application from the question (2 when it names none).

views.name: v_anchor_deviations
views.description: A trip: a stretch of fewer than hold_weeks weeks in which a number's anchor is a different cell site, which is not reported as a move. hold_weeks is set by the application from the question (2 when it names none). CELL SITES, NOT POSITIONS OF A PERSON.

columns.name: number
columns.description: The number.

columns.name: slot
columns.description: night or day.

columns.name: cell_key
columns.description: The cell site that was the anchor during the trip.

columns.name: first_week
columns.description: First week of the trip.

columns.name: last_week
columns.description: Last week of the trip.

columns.name: weeks
columns.description: Weeks of the trip (fewer than hold_weeks).

columns.name: hold_weeks
columns.description: The weeks a stretch needs to count as a move, set by the application from the question (2 when it names none).

views.name: v_anchor_runs
views.description: The stretches of consecutive weeks (those that have an anchor) in which a number has the same anchor in a slot, with whether the stretch holds for at least hold_weeks weeks (set by the application from the question; 2 when it names none): never compute on it yourself. A helper for the anchors, the moves and the trips.

columns.name: number
columns.description: The number.

columns.name: slot
columns.description: night or day.

columns.name: cell_key
columns.description: The anchor cell site of the stretch.

columns.name: first_week
columns.description: First week of the stretch (counted from the start of the case).

columns.name: last_week
columns.description: Last week of the stretch.

columns.name: weeks
columns.description: Number of weeks with this anchor in the stretch (weeks without an anchor do not break it and do not count).

columns.name: holds
columns.description: True when the stretch has at least hold_weeks weeks.

columns.name: hold_weeks
columns.description: The weeks a stretch needs to count as an anchor, set by the application from the question (2 when it names none).

views.name: v_cells
views.description: Cell sites known to the case: name, position and the stated coverage radius. The case's own list wins, then the tenant-wide one; for a cell neither describes, the position is the average of the positions the records themselves give it (no name, and a radius only if the records state one). A cell is not a position of a person; show the radius with any location claim.

views.name: v_colocation_windows
views.description: Windows in which two numbers of the same operator were at the same cell site within a number of minutes of each other (window_minutes; a difference of exactly that many minutes counts); event pairs on one cell are merged into a window while each pair starts within that many minutes of the window's latest time. The number of minutes is set by the application from the question (15 when the question names none): never filter or compute on minutes yourself. Always write a = ... AND b = ... for the two numbers. Proximity is not association; no chance baseline is computed.

columns.name: b

columns.name: end_utc

views.name: v_connection_edges
views.description: How two numbers are connected, through calls and messages in either direction, within three links: ask for a pair with a = first number AND b = second number. Each row is one link (src to dst) of a path from a to b; hops is how many links the path has (1 direct, 2 through one shared contact, 3 through two numbers); ordinary is true when no link of the path goes to a service or through a number everyone contacts; rank_any = 1 marks the shortest paths, rank_ordinary = 1 the shortest ordinary paths. Use for connected, connection, path, link, chain, route, shared contact, how are A and B related, within N hops (up to 3).

columns.name: a
columns.description: The first number of the pair asked about: always write a = '...' in the query.

columns.name: b
columns.description: The second number of the pair asked about: always write b = '...' in the query.

columns.name: src
columns.description: One end of a link of a path from a to b.

columns.name: dst
columns.description: The other end of that link.

columns.name: hops
columns.description: Number of links of the path the row belongs to: 1 direct contact, 2 through one shared contact, 3 through two numbers.

columns.name: ordinary
columns.description: True when no link of the path goes to a service or through a number everyone contacts; use it when the question leaves services and hubs out.

columns.name: rank_any
columns.description: 1 for the shortest paths between a and b, 2 for the next length, and so on.

columns.name: rank_ordinary
columns.description: 1 for the shortest ORDINARY paths (null for a path that is not ordinary); use rank_ordinary = 1 with ordinary when services and hubs are left out.

views.name: v_contact_links

columns.name: events

views.name: v_contact_pairs

views.name: v_rhythm_changes
views.description: For a number, the day on which its daily count of events changed for good: the daily counts (days with no event counted as zero, from its first to its last day) are split at every day that leaves at least min_side_days on each side, the split with the largest absolute Welch t is the change point, and it is listed when |t| is at least 5 and the larger daily mean is at least ratio_percent / 100 times the smaller. min_side_days and ratio_percent are set by the application from the question (10 and 150 when it names none). A CHANGE IN THE PATTERN OF USE, NOT AN EXPLANATION; a short series can show a change by chance.

columns.name: number
columns.description: The number whose rhythm changed.

columns.name: days
columns.description: Days from its first to its last day with an event.

columns.name: first_day
columns.description: The first day of the new rhythm.

columns.name: mean_before
columns.description: Mean events a day before that day.

columns.name: mean_after
columns.description: Mean events a day from that day on.

columns.name: t
columns.description: Welch t of the two sides (empty when the sides have no spread at all).

columns.name: ratio
columns.description: The larger mean divided by the smaller (empty when the smaller is zero).

columns.name: direction
columns.description: up when the daily count rose, down when it fell.

columns.name: min_side_days
columns.description: The fewest days on each side of a change point, set by the application from the question (10 when it names none).

columns.name: ratio_percent
columns.description: The least ratio of the two means, in percent, set by the application from the question (150 when it names none).

A cell site is a coverage area, so an alert may be a handover between towers, a fault or a record error: CELL SITES, NOT POSITIONS OF A PERSON.

columns.name: to_cell_key
columns.description: The cell site of the later event.

columns.name: distance_km

columns.name: gap_s
columns.description: Seconds between the two events.

columns.name: speed_kmh
columns.description: Distance divided by the time, in kilometres per hour; empty when the two events are in the same second.

columns.name: limit_kmh

views.name: v_successor_candidates
views.description: For a number that went silent (old_number) the numbers that may have taken over from it (new_number): a number whose first event is from a few days before to window_days after the old number's last event and that was not in use at the start of the case, with a documented score from three features: contact similarity, shared places and a shared handset. BEHAVIOURAL SIMILARITY, NOT IDENTITY. The silence, the window and the lowest score are set by the application from the question (7 days, 14 days and 35 percent when it names none): never compute on them yourself. Ask with old_number = ... or new_number = ....

columns.name: old_number
columns.description: The number that went silent. Ask with old_number = ... to see who may have taken over from it.

columns.name: new_number
columns.description: A number that started about when the old number stopped and may have taken over from it. Ask with new_number = ... to see which silent number it may have replaced.

columns.name: old_last_event_utc
columns.description: Time of the last event of the old number, UTC (shown on the case clock).

columns.name: new_first_event_utc
columns.description: Time of the first event of the new number, UTC (shown on the case clock).

columns.name: score
columns.description: Documented similarity score from 0 to 1: 0.6 times the contact similarity, 0.2 times the shared places, 0.2 when they share a handset. Not a probability and not identity.

columns.name: contact_cosine
columns.description: Similarity from 0 to 1 of the people the old number contacted in its last days and the new number contacted in its first days (the two numbers themselves left out).

columns.name: shared_contacts
columns.description: Number of people contacted by both.

columns.name: cell_jaccard
columns.description: Share from 0 to 1 of the cell sites that both used at least twice in those periods.

columns.name: shared_device
columns.description: True when the two numbers were used with the same handset (the first 14 digits of the IMEI) at any time.

columns.name: silence_days
columns.description: The days of silence this row was computed with, set by the application from the question (7 when it names none).

columns.name: window_days
columns.description: The days after the old number's last event within which the new number must have started, set by the application from the question (14 when it names none).

columns.name: score_percent
columns.description: The lowest score listed, in percent, set by the application from the question (35 when it names none).

views.name: v_weekly_anchors
views.description: Per number, slot (night: the cell site with most events between 22:00 and 07:00; day: between 09:00 and 17:00 on weekdays, on the case clock) and week (a block of 7 days counted from the start of the case, which is the first day with an event), the cell site with most events of the slot, kept when it has at least min_events events that week (ties: the lowest cell key). The minimum is set by the application from the question (3 when it names none): never compute on it yourself. CELL SITES, NOT POSITIONS OF A PERSON.

columns.name: number
columns.description: The number (the subscriber whose records these are).

columns.name: slot
columns.description: night (22:00 to 07:00) or day (09:00 to 17:00 on weekdays), on the case clock.

columns.name: week
columns.description: Week number counted from the start of the case in blocks of 7 days: 0 is the first week.

columns.name: week_start
columns.description: The date on which the week starts.

columns.name: cell_key
columns.description: The cell site with most events of the slot that week (the anchor).

columns.name: events_at_anchor
columns.description: Events of the slot at that cell site that week.

columns.name: events_in_slot
columns.description: Events of the slot that week at all cell sites.

columns.name: min_events
columns.description: The fewest events of the slot a week needs to have an anchor, set by the application from the question (3 when it names none).

columns.name: site_name
columns.description: Name of the cell site when the case has a reference row for it.

columns.name: lat
columns.description: Latitude of the cell site when known (the site, not the person).

columns.name: lon
columns.description: Longitude of the cell site when known (the site, not the person).
